blocks.content: These fields add context to the notification so the person reading it knows what happened and what to do. The GUI marks them as optional, but if you leave them empty, the responder only sees the alert name and has no idea what happened.
To configure notification context, complete the following steps:
In the alert GUI, scroll to **Section 6: Configure notification message**.

blocks.targetvalue: CPU usage is high on server-01
blocks.content:
In the **Summary** field, enter a short summary of what happened and why.

Example: `CPU usage is high on server-01`

blocks.targetvalue: Fires when CPU exceeds 80% for more than 5 minutes
blocks.content:
In the **Description** field, describe what the alert rule does.

Example: `Fires when CPU exceeds 80% for more than 5 minutes`

In the **Runbook URL** field, enter a link to your team's runbook for this alert.

Example: `https://wiki.example.com/runbooks/high-cpu`
Skip **+ Add custom annotation** and **Link dashboard and panel** for now.
Your notification now includes the context responders need. Next, you'll save the alert rule.
